legend: A schoolboy named Vasya loves reading books on programming and mathematics. He has recently read an encyclopedia article that described the method of median smoothing (or median filter) and its many applications in science and engineering. Vasya liked the idea of the method very much, and he decided to try it in practice.
Applying the simplest variant of median smoothing to the sequence of numbers a1, a2, ..., an will result a new sequence b1, b2, ..., bn obtained by the following algorithm:
b1 = a1, bn = an, that is, the first and the last number of the new sequence match the corresponding numbers of the original sequence.
For i = 2, ..., n - 1 value bi is equal to the median of three values ai - 1, ai and ai + 1.

The median of a set of three numbers is the number that goes on the second place, when these three numbers are written in the non-decreasing order. For example, the median of the set 5, 1, 2 is number 2, and the median of set 1, 0, 1 is equal to 1.
In order to make the task easier, Vasya decided to apply the method to sequences consisting of zeros and ones only.

Having made the procedure once, Vasya looked at the resulting sequence and thought: what if I apply the algorithm to it once again, and then apply it to the next result, and so on? Vasya tried a couple of examples and found out that after some number of median smoothing algorithm applications the sequence can stop changing. We say that the sequence is stable, if it does not change when the median smoothing is applied to it.

Now Vasya wonders, whether the sequence always eventually becomes stable. He asks you to write a program that, given a sequence of zeros and ones, will determine whether it ever becomes stable. Moreover, if it ever becomes stable, then you should determine what will it look like and how many times one needs to apply the median smoothing algorithm to initial sequence in order to obtain a stable one.
input: The first input line of the input contains a single integer n (3 ≤ n ≤ 500 000) — the length of the initial sequence.
The next line contains n integers a1, a2, ..., an (ai = 0 or ai = 1), giving the initial sequence itself.
output: If the sequence will never become stable, print a single number  - 1.

Otherwise, first print a single integer — the minimum number of times one needs to apply the median smoothing algorithm to the initial sequence before it becomes is stable. In the second line print n numbers separated by a space  — the resulting sequence itself.
note: In the second sample the stabilization occurs in two steps: ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/5a983e7baab048cbe43812cb997c15e9d7100231.png), and the sequence 00000 is obviously stable.

legend.ai: 一个名叫 Vasya 的男孩喜欢阅读有关编程和数学的书籍。最近，他读到了一篇介绍中值平滑（或中值滤波）方法及其在科学和工程领域中众多应用的百科全书文章。Vasya 非常喜欢这种方法的思想，于是决定亲自尝试一下。
对数字序列 a1, a2, ..., an 应用最简单形式的中值平滑后，将按照以下算法得到一个新的序列 b1, b2, ..., bn：
b1 = a1，bn = an，也就是说，新序列的第一个和最后一个数字分别与原序列中对应的数字相同。
对于 i = 2, ..., n - 1，bi 的值等于三个数 ai - 1、ai 和 ai + 1 的中位数。
三个数的中位数是指将这三个数按非递减顺序排列后位于第二位的数。例如，集合 5、1、2 的中位数是 2，而集合 1、0、1 的中位数等于 1。
为了使问题更加简单，Vasya 决定只对仅由 0 和 1 组成的序列应用该方法。
执行一次该过程后，Vasya 看着得到的序列，想到：如果再次对它应用该算法，然后再对下一次得到的结果应用该算法，如此反复，会怎样呢？Vasya 尝试了几个例子，发现经过若干次中值平滑算法的应用后，序列可能会停止变化。如果对一个序列应用中值平滑后它不发生变化，我们就称该序列是稳定的。
现在 Vasya 想知道，这个序列是否最终一定会变得稳定。他请你编写一个程序：给定一个由 0 和 1 组成的序列，判断它最终是否会变得稳定。此外，如果它最终会变得稳定，还需要确定最终稳定的序列是什么样子，以及需要对初始序列应用多少次中值平滑算法才能得到稳定序列。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 n（3 ≤ n ≤ 500 000）——初始序列的长度。
接下来一行包含 n 个整数 a1, a2, ..., an（ai = 0 或 ai = 1），即初始序列本身。

output.ai: 如果该序列永远不会变得稳定，则输出一个数  - 1。
否则，先输出一个整数——在变为稳定序列之前，需要对初始序列应用中值平滑算法的最少次数。第二行输出 n 个由空格分隔的数——最终得到的稳定序列。

note.ai: 在第二个样例中，稳定化过程需要两步：![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/5a983e7baab048cbe43812cb997c15e9d7100231.png)，序列 00000 显然是稳定的。
